html:
The Bolivian National Revolution began with a rising in La Paz on 9 April 1952, when armed miners and townspeople defeated the army and brought the Revolutionary Nationalist Movement (MNR) to power.

The MNR, led by Víctor Paz Estenssoro, had grown out of anger at defeat in the Chaco War and at the tin barons such as Patiño. In power it gave the vote to all adults, including Indigenous people who could not read; nationalised the big tin mines; and in 1953 broke up the great estates and gave land to the peasants who worked them.

It was one of the deepest revolutions in Latin America before Cuba's. But the state mining company struggled, and the MNR split. In 1964 the army took power. The revolution changed Bolivia, giving the Aymara and Quechua majority land and votes, the start of a road to plurinational Bolivia.
sum: The Bolivian National Revolution began with a rising in La Paz on 9 April 1952, when armed miners and townspeople defeated the army and brought the Revolutionary Nationalist Movement (MNR) to power.
